source_text: Ὢ τοῦ θαύ ματος! Οὔτε ἐλλείπουσι τῷ ἀριθμῷ, οὔτε πλεονα σμὸν ἐπιδέχονται. Ἐὰν εἰς ἑκατὸν αὐτοὺς διέλῃς, τὸν οἰκεῖον ἀριθμὸν οὐκ ἐκβαίνουσιν· ἐὰν εἰς ἓν συν αγάγῃς, τεσσαράκοντα καὶ οὕτω μένουσι, κατὰ τὴν τοῦ πυρὸς φύσιν. Καὶ γὰρ ἐκεῖνο καὶ πρὸς τὸν ἐξ άπτοντα μεταβαίνει, καὶ ὅλον ἐστὶ παρὰ τῷ ἔχοντι· καὶ οἱ τεσσαράκοντα καὶ πάντες εἰσὶν ὁμοῦ, καὶ πάντες εἰσὶ παρ' ἑκάστῳ. Ἡ ἄφθονος εὐεργεσία, ἡ μὴ δαπανωμένη χάρις· ἑτοίμη βοήθεια Χριστιανοῖς, ἐκκλησία μαρτύρων, στρατὸς τροπαιοφόρων, χορὸς δοξολογούντων. Πόσα ἂν ἔκαμες, ἵνα ἕνα που εὕ ρῃς ὑπὲρ σοῦ δυσωποῦντα τὸν Κύριον; Τεσσαράκοντά εἰσι, σύμφωνον ἀναπέμποντες προσευχήν. Ὅπου δύο ἢ τρεῖς εἰσι συνηγμένοι ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Κυρίου, ἐκεῖ ἐστιν ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν. Ὅπου δὲ τεσσαράκοντα, τίς ἀμφιβάλλει Θεοῦ παρουσίαν; Ὁ θλιβόμενος ἐπὶ τοὺς τεσσαράκοντα καταφεύγει, ὁ εὐφραινόμενος ἐπ' αὐτοὺς ἀποτρέχει· ὁ μὲν, ἵνα λύσιν εὕρῃ τῶν δυσχερῶν· ὁ δὲ, ἵνα φυλαχθῇ αὐτῷ τὰ χρηστότερα. Ἐνταῦθα γυνὴ εὐσεβὴς ὑπὲρ τέκνων εὐχομένη καταλαμβάνεται, ἀποδημοῦντι ἀνδρὶ τὴν ἐπάνοδον αἰ τουμένη, ἀῤῥωστοῦντι τὴν σωτηρίαν. Μετὰ μαρτύ ρων γενέσθω τὰ αἰτήματα ὑμῶν. Οἱ νεανίσκοι τοὺς ἡλικιώτας μιμείσθωσαν· οἱ πατέρες, τοιούτων εἶναι παίδων πατέρες εὐχέσθωσαν· αἱ μητέρες, καλῆς μητρὸς διήγημα διδαχθήτωσαν. Μήτηρ ἑνὸς τῶν μακαρίων ἐκείνων, θεασαμένη τοὺς ἄλλους ἤδη τῷ κρύει τελειωθέντας, τὸν δὲ ἑαυτῆς υἱὸν ἔτι ἐμπνέοντα ὑπό τε ῥώμης καὶ τῆς πρὸς τὰ δεινὰ καρτερίας, καταλιμπανόντων αὐτὸν τῶν δημίων ὡς δυ νάμενόν γε μεταβουλεύσασθαι, αὐτὴ ταῖς οἰκείαις χερσὶν ἀραμένη, ἐπέθηκε τῇ ἁμάξῃ, ἐφ' ἧς οἱ λοιποὶ συγκείμενοι πρὸς τὴν πυρὰν ἤγοντο, μάρτυρος ὄντως μήτηρ. Οὐ γὰρ δάκρυον ἀφῆκεν ἀγεννές· οὐδ' ἐφθέγξατο ταπεινόν τι καὶ ἀνάξιον τοῦ καιροῦ· ἀλλ', Ἄπιθι, φησὶν, ὦ παῖ, τὴν ἀγαθὴν πορείαν μετὰ τῶν ἡλικιωτῶν, μετὰ τῶν συσκήνων· μὴ ἀπολειφθῇς τῆς χορείας· μὴ δεύτερος τῶν ἄλλων ἐμφανισθῇς τῷ Δεσπότῃ. Ὄντως ἀγαθῆς ῥίζης ἀγαθὸν βλάστημα. Ἔδειξεν ἡ γενναία μήτηρ, ὅτι δόγμασιν εὐσεβείας ἐξέθρεψεν αὐτὸν μᾶλλον ἢ γάλακτι. Καὶ ὁ μὲν οὕτω τραφεὶς οὕτω προεπ έμφθη παρὰ μητρὸς εὐσεβοῦς· ὁ δὲ διάβολος ἀπῆλθε κατ ησχυμμένος. Ἅπασαν γὰρ ἐπ' αὐτοὺς κινήσας τὴν κτίσιν, πάντα εὗρεν ἡττώμενα τῆς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἀρε τῆς, νύκτα δυσήνεμον, πατρίδα χειμέριον, τὴν ὥραν τοῦ ἔτους, τῶν σωμάτων τὴν γύμνωσιν. Ὢ χορὸς ἅγιος! ὢ σύνταγμα ἱερόν! ὢ συνασπισμὸς ἀῤ ῥαγής! ὢ κοινοὶ φύλακες τοῦ γένους τῶν ἀνθρώ πων! ἀγαθοὶ κοινωνοὶ φροντίδων, δεήσεως συνεργοὶ, πρεσβευταὶ δυνατώτατοι, ἀστέρες τῆς οἰκουμέ νης, ἄνθη τῶν Ἐκκλησιῶν. Ὑμᾶς οὐχ ἡ γῆ κατέκρυψεν, ἀλλ' οὐρανὸς ὑπεδέξατο· ἠνοίγησαν ὑμῖν παραδείσου πύλαι. Ἄξιον θέαμα τῇ στρατιᾷ τῶν ἀγγέλων, ἄξιον πατριάρχαις, προφήταις, δικαίοις, ἄνδρες ἐν αὐτῷ τῷ ἄνθει τῆς νεότητος, τοῦ βίου καταφρονήσαντες, ὑπὲρ γονεῖς, ὑπὲρ τέκνα τὸν Κύριον ἀγαπήσαντες. Αὐτὸ τῆς ἡλικίας ἄγοντες τὸ βιώσιμον, ὑπερεῖδον τῆς προσκαίρου ζωῆς, ἵνα δοξά σωσι τὸν Θεὸν ἐν τοῖς μέλεσιν ἑαυτῶν· θέατρον γενόμενοι τῷ κόσμῳ, καὶ ἀγγέλοις, καὶ ἀνθρώποις, τοὺς πεπτωκότας ἤγειραν, τοὺς ἀμφιβόλους ἐβεβαιώ σαντο, τοῖς εὐσεβέσι τὴν ἐπιθυμίαν ἐδιπλασίασαν. Ἒν ὑπὲρ τῆς εὐσεβείας ἅπαντες ἀναστήσαντες τρόπαιον. ἑνὶ καὶ τῷ στεφάνῳ τῆς δικαιοσύνης κατεκοσμήθησαν, ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ Κυρίῳ ἡμῶν, ᾧ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: The Forty as inexhaustible intercessors and the mother's noble deed
orientation: Basil is closing the homily by praising the Forty Martyrs as ever-present helpers and telling the story of the mother who placed her still-living son on the cart to the pyre.
pass_a_gloss: O the wonder! Neither do they fall short in number, nor do they admit increase. If you divide them into a hundred, they do not go beyond their own number; if you gather them into one, they remain forty even so, according to the nature of fire. For that also passes to the one who kindles it, and is whole with the one who has it; and the forty both are all together, and are all with each one. The ungrudging beneficence, the grace that is not spent; ready help for Christians, church of martyrs, army of trophy-bearers, company of those who glorify. How much would you have toiled, in order that you might find somewhere one entreating the Lord on your behalf? They are forty, sending up a harmonious prayer. Where two or three are gathered in the name of the Lord, there He is in the midst of them. But where forty are, who doubts the presence of God? The one who is afflicted flees for refuge to the forty, the one who rejoices runs to them; the one, in order that he may find release from difficulties; the other, in order that better things may be kept safe for him. Here a devout woman praying for children is overtaken, asking the return of a husband who is away, the salvation of one who is sick. Let your requests be made with martyrs. Let the young men imitate those of their own age; let fathers pray to be fathers of such children; let mothers be taught the story of the noble mother. The mother of one of those blessed ones, having seen the others already perfected by the cold, but her own son still breathing because of strength and endurance against terrible things, the executioners leaving him behind as being able indeed to change his mind, she herself having lifted him with her own hands, placed him on the cart, on which the rest having been laid were being carried to the pyre, truly a mother of a martyr. For she did not let fall an ignoble tear; nor did she utter anything lowly and unworthy of the occasion; but, 'Go,' she says, 'O child, on the good journey with those of your own age, with your tent-companions; do not be left behind from the company; do not appear second to the others before the Master.' Truly a good shoot of a good root. The noble mother showed that she nourished him with the teachings of devotion rather than with milk. And the one so reared was thus sent forth by his devout mother; and the devil went away put to shame. For having stirred all creation against them, he found all things defeated by the virtue of the men: the stormy night, the wintry homeland, the season of the year, the nakedness of their bodies. O holy company! O sacred band! O unbroken shield-wall! O common guardians of the race of men! Good sharers of cares, co-workers of supplication, most powerful ambassadors, stars of the inhabited world, flowers of the Churches. The earth did not hide you, but heaven received you; the gates of paradise were opened to you. A sight worthy of the army of angels, worthy of patriarchs, prophets, righteous ones: men in the very flower of youth, having despised life, having loved the Lord above parents, above children. Leading the very livable part of their age, they looked down on the temporary life, in order that they might glorify God in their members; having become a spectacle to the world, and to angels, and to men, they raised up those who had fallen, they strengthened those who were doubtful, they doubled the desire of the devout. All having raised one trophy for devotion, with one crown also of righteousness they were adorned, in Christ Jesus our Lord, to whom be the glory and the might unto the ages of ages. Amen.

choices.term: Ἡ ἄφθονος εὐεργεσία, ἡ μὴ δαπανωμένη χάρις
choices.english: The ungrudging beneficence, the grace that is not spent
choices.why: ἄφθονος means without envy or grudge, not merely abundant; δαπανωμένη is passive of δαπανάω, to be used up or spent, preserving the economic metaphor of inexhaustible grace
rejected: The abundant kindness, the grace that is not consumed
The generous benefaction, the unspent favor

choices.why: στρατός is army, and τροπαιοφόρος means bearing trophies of victory; keeps the military register Basil uses for the martyrs
σύμφωνος means in agreement or harmonious; ἀναπέμπω is to send up, preserving the upward direction of prayer

choices.english: asking the return of a husband who is away
choices.why: ἀποδημέω means to be away from home or traveling; ἐπάνοδος is return; the dative participles mark the persons for whom the woman prays
rejected: asking the return of a husband who is abroad
requesting the homecoming of a traveling husband

choices.english: the salvation of one who is sick
choices.why: σωτηρία is salvation or deliverance, not specifically healing; ἀρρωστέω means to be sick or weak; the woman asks for the sick person's deliverance
rejected: the healing of one who is sick

choices.why: συνασπισμός is the locking of shields in battle formation; ἀρραγής means unbroken or unbreakable; preserves the military image

bible_refs.note: Ὅπου δύο ἢ τρεῖς εἰσι συνηγμένοι ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Κυρίου, ἐκεῖ ἐστιν ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν

pass_b_english: What a wonder! They do not fall short in number, nor do they admit any increase. If you divide them into a hundred, they do not leave their proper number; if you gather them into one, they remain forty, just as fire behaves. For fire passes to the one who lights from it, and yet remains whole with the one who has it; so the Forty are all together, and all are present with each one. This is ungrudging beneficence, grace that is not spent, ready help for Christians, a church of martyrs, an army of trophy-bearers, a company of those who glorify God. How much would you have toiled to find even one person to entreat the Lord on your behalf? Here are forty, sending up a harmonious prayer. Where two or three are gathered in the name of the Lord, there He is in the midst of them (Matthew 18:20). Where there are forty, who can doubt the presence of God? The one who is afflicted flees for refuge to the Forty; the one who rejoices runs to them—the one, to find release from hardships; the other, to keep his blessings secure. Here a devout woman praying for her children is heard, asking the return of a husband who is away, the salvation of one who is sick. Let your requests be made with the martyrs. Let the young men imitate those of their own age; let fathers pray to be fathers of such children; let mothers learn from the story of a noble mother. The mother of one of those blessed ones, seeing the others already perfected by the cold, while her own son was still breathing because of his strength and endurance of terrible things, and seeing the executioners leaving him behind as one who might change his mind, lifted him with her own hands and placed him on the cart on which the rest were laid and carried to the pyre—a true mother of a martyr. For she shed no ignoble tear, nor uttered anything low or unworthy of the moment, but said, “Go, my child, on the good journey with those of your own age, with your tent-companions. Do not be left behind from the company. Do not appear before the Master second to the others.” Truly a good shoot from a good root. The noble mother showed that she had nourished him with the teachings of devotion more than with milk. And the one so raised was thus sent forth by his devout mother; and the devil went away put to shame. For though he had stirred up all creation against them, he found everything defeated by the men’s virtue—the stormy night, the wintry homeland, the season of the year, the nakedness of their bodies. O holy company! O sacred band! O unbroken shield-wall! O common guardians of the human race! Good sharers of cares, co-workers in supplication, most powerful ambassadors, stars of the world, flowers of the churches. The earth did not hide you, but heaven received you; the gates of paradise were opened to you. A sight worthy of the army of angels, worthy of patriarchs, prophets, and the righteous: men in the very flower of youth, despising life, loving the Lord more than parents, more than children. At the very prime of life, they looked with contempt on this passing life, so that they might glorify God in their members; becoming a spectacle to the world, and to angels, and to men, they raised up the fallen, confirmed the wavering, and doubled the desire of the devout. All together they raised one trophy for devotion. With one crown of righteousness they were adorned, in Christ Jesus our Lord, to whom be glory and power forever and ever. Amen.

problems.quote: fire passes to the one who kindles it
problems.source_quote: ἐκεῖνο καὶ πρὸς τὸν ἐξάπτοντα μεταβαίνει
problems.why: Fire passes to the one who kindles FROM it, not the one who kindles it; reverses the direction of fire's transmission.
problems.fix: fire passes to the one who lights from it
problems.ruling: ἐξάπτοντα is active 'kindler/igniter', not passive; fire passes TO the kindler, reversing source meaning.

edits.old: fire passes to the one who kindles it
edits.new: fire passes to the one who lights from it

fixed: Corrected mistranslation: source ἐκεῖνο καὶ πρὸς τὸν ἐξάπτοντα μεταβαίνει means fire passes to the one who kindles from it, not the one who kindles it.

last_rejected.why: χειμέριον means 'wintry/stormy'; πατρίδα here means 'fatherland' but context is Sebaste, not their homeland. Likely 'wintry region' or 'stormy land'.
last_rejected.ruling: πατρίδα = fatherland/homeland; χειμέριον = wintry. 'Wintry homeland' is within normal range; 'region' is mere preference.
